background_notes.fact: For the Fourier multiplier S_t of D005 and every real s, S_t is a linear isometry on H^s, S_t S_r=S_(t+r), and t -> S_t f is continuous in H^s for each f in H^s. Consequently, the N001 solution u in C([0,T];H^gamma) has a continuous twist v(t)=S_(-t)u(t); since gamma>0 it is also L2-continuous. Subtracting the N007 continuous interpolation gives an L2-continuous e, with e(0)=0. The same isometry gives ||S_(-n*tau)(u(n*tau)-u^n)||_2=||u(n*tau)-u^n||_2.

grounds.reason: H^s is the weighted square-sum completion, and L2=H^0.
The exact solution is H^gamma-continuous with the stated initial value.
The numerical interpolation is continuous and matches the grid values.

background_notes.justification: Each multiplier has modulus one and its phases multiply by addition of times, proving the norm and group identities first on polynomials and then on the completion. For strong continuity approximate f by a polynomial: the two tail terms are bounded by twice the approximation error, and the finitely many polynomial coefficients depend continuously on time. For varying u(t), add and subtract S_(-t)u(t0) and use the isometry. The weight (1+k^2)^gamma>=1 gives ||f||_2<=||f||_(H^gamma). Difference continuity, S_0=I and initial endpoint matching give continuity and e(0)=0. The grid identity follows by linearity and isometry.

background_notes.fact: For gamma>0, positive real powers are increasing and (x^(1/gamma))^gamma=x for x>0. With the positive Csm,delta0 chosen in S003, tausm=min(1,delta0/2,(1/(4*(Csm+1)))^(1/gamma)) is positive, and 0<tau<=tausm implies Csm*tau^gamma<=Csm/(4*(Csm+1))<1/4.

grounds.reason: delta0>0 and K0>0 are available jointly.
Bcount is a positive integer and Csm=K0*delta0*(2^Bcount-1)>0.

background_notes.justification: For positive x, x^gamma=exp(gamma*log(x)); monotonicity and inverse identities for log and exp give the stated power facts. Every entry of the finite minimum is positive. Raising tau<= (1/(4*(Csm+1)))^(1/gamma) to gamma yields the claimed estimate, whose strict inequality follows from Csm/(Csm+1)<1.

background_notes.fact: If e:[0,T]->L2 is continuous, T>0 and e(0)=0, then g(t)=||e(t)||_2 is continuous and has a maximum on every compact initial interval. If g reaches 1, there is a first time t*>0 with g(t*)=1 and g(t)<=1 for 0<=t<=t*. If it never reaches 1, then g(t)<1 everywhere and max_[0,T] g<1.

grounds.reason: The paths constructed from N001 and N007 give continuous e and e(0)=0, as checked in BG001.
L2 temporarily assumes the level 1 is attained.

background_notes.justification: The reverse triangle inequality makes the norm continuous. A continuous real function on a compact interval attains its extrema. Under L2 its nonempty level set at 1 is closed and compact, hence has a least time, positive because g(0)=0. Any earlier value greater than 1 would produce an earlier value 1 by the intermediate value theorem. If the level set is empty, the same theorem rules out values above 1; compactness then makes the attained maximum strictly less than 1. These facts justify exactly the displayed first-time bootstrap contradiction.
